node.label: Eric Foner
node.date_label: Free Soil, Free Labor, Free Men (1970) · Reconstruction: America’s Unfinished Revolution (1988) · The Story of American Freedom (1998)
node.description: A historian of emancipation and Reconstruction who places Black political action, contested freedom and federal enforcement at the centre of United States history. He explicitly identifies Du Bois’s account of Reconstruction as a resource while distinguishing war’s destructiveness from emancipation’s consequences.

proposed_edges.relationship: Interprets Reconstruction through Black political action, contested freedom and the struggle to build democracy.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview answers stress change after slavery and oppose treating later injustice as proof that emancipation changed nothing.

proposed_edges.relationship: Traces competing meanings of freedom rather than treating freedom as one stable national possession.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: In the interview Foner explicitly contrasts economic equality and rights with narrow anti-government definitions, and rejects narratives that absorb every struggle into a stable Americanism.
